description: Replay of a remembered argument. `coder` cases are single turns with the moves that would be acceptable. `replays` run the real loop: two rehearsal avatars built from each person's usable lines take turns from the agreed opening line, and every turn is coded. Checked on every generated turn: schema and guardrail pass, short, nothing about being an avatar or a simulation, and none of that person's `must_not_say` patterns (their settled requirement given up, or a line marked act-on-but-never-say spoken aloud). Checked on the whole: it does not make peace at once. Recognition against each person's remembered moves is printed, not gated: that verdict belongs to the two people.

frame.label: The card statement in March
frame.setting: A weeknight, in the kitchen, just after Ben got home
frame.openingLine: Can we go through the card statement tonight? There's a charge on it I don't recognize.

people.name: Ben

entries.text: Security comes first. Saving matters more to me than almost anything.
Ana and I never hide anything about money from each other.
I bought bike parts and didn't tell Ana for weeks.
I check the joint account most mornings.
When money comes up I explain myself at length before I ask anything, and then I go quiet for the rest of the evening.
That one bad year puts us where my parents were, losing the house.
Telling Ana about a purchase before I make it, not after.
That Ana thinks less of me every time this happens.
We lost the house when I was twelve.

people.name: Ana
people.state_before: Had found the charge that afternoon and been turning it over for hours. Calm on the surface, not underneath.

entries.text: Being able to say anything to each other matters more to me than being comfortable.
We don't go to bed without at least saying where we each are, even if it isn't solved.
When Ben goes quiet I follow him from room to room until he talks.
I raise things the moment I notice them, usually while he's in the middle of something else.
That silence means he's already decided to leave.
Giving Ben the hour he asks for without knocking on the door.
My parents never shouted. They left the room and it was silent for days.
